g1.label: 1. ___ small hotel near the river
g1.why: First mention of the hotel — we don't know which one yet, so use the indefinite article "a".

g2.label: 2. ___ Egyptian collection
g2.why: The British Museum has one specific Egyptian collection — both speaker and listener know which one, so use "the".

g3.label: 3. ___ ice cream in the park
g3.why: First mention of an unspecified ice cream. Use "an" because "ice" starts with a vowel sound.

g4.label: 4. ___ Oxford Street
g4.why: Street names normally take no article. "Oxford Street", not "the Oxford Street".

g5.label: 5. ___ book about London's history
g5.why: First mention of an unspecified book — the reader hasn't heard about this book before, so use "a".

g6.label: 6. ___ musical in the West End
g6.why: First mention of an unspecified musical — one of many in the West End, not a particular one.

g1.label: 1. There is ___ new café
g1.why: Introducing the café for the first time — use "a" for first mention.

g2.label: 1. ___ café serves great coffee
g2.why: Second mention — now the listener knows which café, so switch to "The".

g3.label: 2. She wants to be ___ engineer
g3.why: Jobs use the indefinite article: "an engineer", "a doctor". Use "an" before the vowel sound in "engineer".

g4.label: 3. Can you close ___ window?
g4.why: Both speaker and listener can see the specific window — use "the" for shared knowledge.

g5.label: 4. I saw ___ dog in the park
g5.why: First mention of an unspecified dog — the listener doesn't know which dog yet.

g6.label: 4. It was chasing ___ ball
g6.why: First mention of an unspecified ball — introduced for the first time, so use "a".

g7.label: 5. My brother is ___ tallest person
g7.why: Superlatives always take "the" — there can only be one tallest.

g8.label: 6. I need to buy ___ umbrella
g8.why: Any umbrella, not a specific one — use "an" before the vowel sound in "umbrella".

g1.label: 1. ___ Water is essential for life
g1.why: Water in general, not specific water — uncountable nouns used generally take no article.

g2.label: 2. ___ water in this bottle
g2.why: "in this bottle" specifies exactly which water — use "the" for identified things.

g3.label: 3. She loves ___ music
g3.why: Music in general — no article with uncountable nouns when talking about the whole category.

g4.label: 4. ___ music at the party
g4.why: "at the party" identifies the specific music — use "the".

g5.label: 5. I usually have ___ breakfast
g5.why: Meals take no article when used in general: "have breakfast", "eat lunch", "go to dinner".

g6.label: 6. ___ breakfast she cooked
g6.why: "she cooked this morning" makes it a specific breakfast — use "the".

g7.label: 7. He goes to ___ school
g7.why: "Go to school" (as a student) is a set phrase with no article — it means the activity, not the building.

g8.label: 8. ___ school on Park Road
g8.why: "on Park Road" identifies a specific school building — use "the".
